findings.statement: Robinhood prediction-market contracts for 'BTC price on Aug 21, 2026 at 5pm EDT' (resolution source: CF Benchmarks RTI) imply the following cumulative probabilities (market prices shown as cents = %): P(BTC ≥ $62,500) = 58% (0.58), P(BTC ≥ $63,000) = 48% (0.48), P(BTC ≥ $63,500) = 39% (0.39), P(BTC ≥ $64,000) = 31% (0.31).

Robinhood’s 'BTC price range on Aug 21, 2026 at 5pm EDT' event shows nearby 500‑USD buckets priced around 10–11¢ for mid‑$62k–$63k buckets (examples shown on the event page: $62,000–62,499.99 = 11¢; $62,500–62,999.99 = 11¢; $63,000–63,499.99 = 11¢; $63,500–63,999.99 = 10¢). This provides a discrete, crowd‑implied short‑dated distribution that can be converted to an expected value if the full bucket set is retrieved and midpoints are used.

Polymarket runs multiple live Aug 21, 2026 Bitcoin markets (hourly 'Up/Down' markets and daily/dated 'price on [date]' markets). These markets publish bucketed outcome probabilities (example: Polymarket 'Bitcoin price on August 20?' shows 62,000–64,000 = 35%, 64,000–66,000 = 26%, 60,000–62,000 = 20%), demonstrating that prediction markets are producing explicit discrete distributions for Aug 21 time windows as well (hourly markets exist for many hours on Aug 21).

Deribit (options) implied‑volatility surface for BTC shows a marked term/strike structure for expiries around Aug 21, 2026: third‑party IV surface snapshots (Pandabull) list ATM/near‑ATM IVs for 21AUG26 with ATM IVs in the mid‑20s% (Pandabull snapshot: '21AUG26' row shows ATM/ATM‑like IV ≈ 23.78% and quoted 'Latest' 24.40% for the expiry), and deeper-dated expiries show higher IV. This establishes the market pricing of expected volatility for the Aug 21 expiry.

Deribit’s own documentation (Deribit Insights / DVOL and option‑discovery materials) describes the method the exchange uses to compute an implied forward for each expiry (using option mid‑prices/synthetic/future mark when available) and explains that, given options market prices across strikes, one can construct a risk‑neutral / implied distribution for the underlying at expiry (Deribit publishes the algorithmic approach used to compute the implied forward and to select strikes for the IV surface).

Programmatic access / data‑access notes for the market‑implied sources found: (a) Deribit provides public market‑data websocket/REST endpoints (index feeds and option quotes) via its API (docs publicly available) for programmatic retrieval of option prices and synthetic forward marks; (b) third‑party IV surface tools (e.g., Pandabull) scrape/aggregate Deribit and present per‑expiry IV pillars (no guarantee of commercial SLA); (c) Polymarket exposes market pages (public web) for each event (no documented free historical bulk API — data extraction typically done by web/API clients); (d) Robinhood prediction pages are web‑facing but some endpoints require login; Robinhood explicitly states CF Benchmarks RTI is the resolution source for its event(s).

I could not find any publicly‑available, reputable institutional or sell‑side research note that publishes an exact point forecast for Bitcoin's closing price specifically on 2026‑08‑21 (single‑day point forecasts from banks/asset managers are typically not published for a particular calendar date; available institutional commentary instead gives ranges, scenarios or monthly/quarterly targets).

final_answer.answer:
Short answer: I cannot (on the basis of the validated research provided) produce a single, fully‑justified exact Bitcoin closing price for next Friday (the target calendar date is 2026‑08‑21). The available sources contain partial market‑implied information (prediction‑market buckets and options implied volatility) but do not supply a complete, citable probability distribution or a chosen benchmark/endpoint required to compute and justify an exact point forecast.

Why not (brief):
- Robinhood prediction markets provide threshold contracts and 500‑USD buckets for an event labeled “BTC price on Aug 21, 2026 at 5pm EDT,” and those buckets/thresholds imply market probabilities in the low‑tens of cents in the mid‑$62k–$63k area (examples: P(BTC ≥ $62,500)=58%, P(BTC ≥ $63,000)=48%, P(BTC ≥ $63,500)=39%, P(BTC ≥ $64,000)=31%; example buckets priced ~10–11¢ for $62k–$63.5k ranges). Those partial examples show crowd‑implied mass near $62–64k but are not a full bucket set you can sum to an exact expectation here (Robinhood pages also state they resolve to CF Benchmarks RTI). (Sources: S25, S26)
- Polymarket likewise runs dated and hourly BTC markets that publish discrete bucket probabilities for date‑specific windows (examples exist for Aug 20/21), but we do not have the complete Aug 21 bucketed distribution here. Without the full bucket list + probabilities you cannot compute a verified expected value. (Source: S27)
- Options markets provide the information needed to build an implied (risk‑neutral) distribution, and third‑party snapshots show materially positive IV for the 21AUG26 expiry (Pandabull shows ATM/near‑ATM IV ≈ 23.8% / “Latest” ~24.4%). Deribit documents how to derive an implied forward / distribution from option prices, but the research set contains IV snapshots and documentation only — not a computed implied‑forward price for Aug 21 that we can cite as a single point forecast. (Sources: S28, S29)
- No reputable institutional or sell‑side note in the collected research publishes an exact single‑day point forecast for the 2026‑08‑21 close; analysts typically publish ranges or scenario targets rather than a single closing price on a calendar day. (Sources: S30, S31)

What would be required to produce a justified exact point forecast (so I can do it if you want):
- Obtain the full set of Robinhood range buckets and their market prices/probabilities for the “Aug 21 5pm EDT” event (the page examples in the research are partial). Robinhood pages identify CF Benchmarks RTI as the resolution source, so that specific snapshot could be used to define what “closing price” means for that event. (Sources: S25, S26)
- Or obtain the full Polymarket bucket distribution for an Aug 21 market (daily or hour‑aligned) and compute the expectation from bucket midpoints and probabilities. (Source: S27)
- Or retrieve Deribit option quotes (via Deribit’s public API) for the 21AUG26 expiry and compute an implied forward / risk‑neutral distribution per Deribit’s documented methodology, then report the implied‑forward as a point forecast. (Source: S29)

If you want an exact numeric forecast with full justification, tell me which approach you prefer (use Robinhood buckets resolved to CF Benchmarks RTI at 5pm EDT; Polymarket daily/hourly buckets; or an options‑implied forward from Deribit), and I will fetch and compute the expectation from the complete data set you authorize me to use. The sources above show that each approach is feasible, but the validated research here is incomplete for producing the single figure you requested. (Sources: S25, S26, S27, S28, S29)
